name: Sungnyemun
description: Sungnyemun (also known as South Gate) is a city gate in the center of Seoul, the capital of South Korea. It was built in 1398 in the Ming Dynasty and is located in Jung-gu, Seoul. Known as the national gate of South Korea, it was designated as South Korea's No. 1 national treasure on December 20, 1962. It is the spiritual symbol of all Korean people. Sungnyemun Gate was the largest of the four gates in Seoul in the early years. It is also the oldest remaining wooden building in Seoul. The lower end of the city gate is a stone doorway, and the upper end is a double-story wooden tower. In 2008, the wooden two-story pavilion was burned down by arson, leaving only the stone foundation. Reconstruction began in May of the same year. The Korean Cultural Heritage Administration said on the 21st that the Sungnyemun Gate reconstruction project was completed on April 30, 2013.
